## ZCode candidate independence

OV-027/OV-029 select the isolated candidate, with later owner direction removing ZCode login,
startup questionnaires, marketing artwork, purchase/upgrade UI and official collection dependencies.
This section describes `.fleet/zcode`; the retained Craft service inventory below is not evidence
for this candidate. Source changes retire WelcomeScreen/automatic questionnaire mounting and purchase
dialogs, use local provider settings, disable official updates/ARMS and cloud rollout/help fetching,
and reject product account/billing/config requests before the Node transport. User-selected model
API endpoints remain separate. The manual local preference guide has no vendor artwork or survey
submission. No replacement cloud service or data migration is added.

`test:fleet-local` verifies rejected product endpoints (including configured override), no telemetry
identity/state/transport collection, local help configuration and local profile persistence.
These are bounded fixtures, not a proof that every process has zero network traffic. GitHub MCP/plugin
scope is recorded in [marketplace](marketplace.md#github-package-and-official-implementations);
real authorization and owner visual acceptance are still outstanding. The inherited plugin store no longer triggers a ZCode CDN refresh merely on opening; explicit refresh remains an optional third-party catalog operation. Existing remote/community,
cloud sharing and other inherited features require their own endpoint audit before release.

### Candidate local Help and Agent guide

`packages/ui/src/lib/productDocs.ts` imports the same English/Chinese Markdown files packaged in
`apps/zcode-cli/packages/zcode-guide-plugin/docs/`. Help and quick-pick use the existing Markdown
preview pane; no hosted document request or second reader is added. Vendor community, feedback and
feature-request entries are retired from Help/quick-pick. The owner limits Help to **Help documentation,
Resource Manager and Check for Updates**. OV-041 also adds Software update to the avatar menu;
both share `DesktopUpdateMenuItem`, the existing updater state and command. Local log export and About remain native menu actions.
The updater reports unavailable before network I/O until a Fleet feed exists; it never uses the old
ZCode feed. The in-app About content identifies Fleet while retaining attribution; the dev app/menu
still exposes the upstream ZCode identity. A distributable rename requires bundle/signing, protocol
and profile-migration acceptance before it can be called complete.

The owner also rejected the current single-summary guide design. Bundling that summary proves only
offline delivery, not the required documentation experience or completeness. Compare the retained
Craft topic menu, `LocalHelpOverlay.tsx`, `DocumentFormattedMarkdownOverlay.tsx` and local article/link
mapping before replacing the candidate reader. Adapt article contents to ZCode/Fleet's actual
configuration owners; copying Craft-specific paths and schemas would give the Agent incorrect
instructions. The owner prioritizes Agent-required configuration instructions over a generic usage summary;
Craft-style small conversations are confirmed. Further scope must come from source evidence, not
another request for the owner to design the feature.

The existing `zcode-guide@zcode-plugins-official` identity, enable/disable and suppression state remain
owned by plugin discovery. Desktop dev/release staging and SEA carry the guide. The owner rejected
the added global `Ask Agent to configure` menu action: attaching a general guide to a new chat does
not implement contextual feature editing. Remove that action and its dispatch path; keep local
reading and the packaged reference skill. Its current guide now follows actual key saves, model-add/test feedback, automatic effort, compact Fast, avatar preferences and ledger statistics; this does not close the rejected single-article experience. Feature-page assistance has its own contract in
[components](components.md#shared-operations-and-contextual-agent-assistance). The guide cannot grant
permissions or authorize an edit. Plugin Creator and Skill Creator retain their existing lifecycle;
this correction does not add native UI-extension APIs or declare those packages fully delivered.

## Outcome

Fleet's core runs and degrades honestly with **zero silent dependence on Craft-operated services**
(Decision P8). Every inherited endpoint is: replaced by a local/user-owned path, kept as an
**explicit optional connector**, or **honestly disabled** with a clear unavailable state. The
binary updater can no longer install a Craft binary over Fleet.

## Walkthrough (system + user)

1. Fresh start, network blocked: app launches; local Projects/sessions/files/permissions/
   labels/tasks/automations work; no error spam from unreachable Craft endpoints; optional
   features show honest "not configured / unavailable" states.
2. The user opens each affected surface and can tell which class every external connection is:
   local · self-hosted · third-party connector · unavailable (identity honesty: a connection says what it actually is).
3. Packaged startup, manual update check and normal quit: either a verified
   Fleet-controlled/user-configured channel, or updates are unavailable before any download or
   install. Dismissing a notification is not disabling the updater. Pending downloaded packages
   must not bypass this boundary on quit.
4. Session sharing: implement the approved local Markdown replacement with conversation content
   and attachment references. Verify the desktop download as well as the RPC. Existing
   published copies retain explicit cleanup; new hosted conversation/Pages publication is refused.

## Scope

One slice per service row from [`../architecture.md`](../architecture.md#code-map) "Craft-operated service
boundaries" — updater, sharing/viewer, help/docs links + docs MCP, WebUI OAuth relay, Slack OAuth
relay, sources/connectors audit, branding/support text (deliberate rename pass with
license/trademark review), telemetry and Pages publication. Trace UI → handler → persistence → recovery per slice; never several
services in one patch.

- **Out (non-goals):** building replacement cloud services; upstream version bump; remote
  execution (P7/P9 — separate); marketing/rename beyond honest identity.
- **Reserved paths:** this spec; credential storage formats.

## Reality anchors and execution order

Audit the actual boundaries listed in `app/apps/electron/src/main/auto-update.ts`,
`app/apps/electron/electron-builder.yml`, `app/packages/shared/src/branding.ts`,
`app/packages/shared/src/auth/`, `app/packages/server-core/src/webui/`, and
`app/apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/ChatPage.tsx`. Execute one service row at a time: trace
renderer → RPC/handler → persistence → recovery, add the row's targeted test, then run
`bun run typecheck:electron` and the relevant shared test from `app/`. The network-blocked smoke
must record the target URL/process log; a code search alone does not prove C1 or C6.

For desktop Claude/ChatGPT subscription login, the inherited proxy manager forced Electron's
default session to direct mode when no app proxy was configured, while token exchange and refresh
used Node `fetch`. Invalid-code probes returned HTTP 403 direct but normal credential errors through
the OS proxy on the review Mac (Claude 400, ChatGPT 401); Claude's direct/system result was also
reproduced with Electron's Chromium fetch. The bounded correction uses an in-memory OAuth-only
Electron session, set to the OS proxy when no app proxy is configured; Craft's default and browser
sessions retain their original policy. Explicit app proxy values, the original OAuth state/credential
owner, cancellation and later setup remain. Real-account login
and refresh still require a user-authenticated acceptance run; the probe alone does not establish
`usable` status.

The ZCode candidate must apply the same subscription network rule: explicit application proxy
and bypass rules win; otherwise the local desktop resolves the OS/PAC route through an isolated
Electron session. The existing Host transport owns dispatch, cancellation and cleanup; Main only
resolves the route and never receives tokens or request bodies. Login, refresh, catalogs and usage
use this route, and each subscription inference request receives its current route through the
existing Host-to-Agent request-material contract. API-key traffic, tool processes and remote hosts
keep their configured network policy. Failed proxy resolution or an unsupported proxy must fail
explicitly, never silently retry directly. No credential-store migration or additional login method.

The original updater has automatic download and quit installation enabled, with the Craft feed.
This is inherited Craft behavior, not a completed Fleet service boundary. Trace launch, manual
check, ignored versions and already-downloaded packages before implementing the approved correction.
Use disposable lifecycle fixtures; do not download/install an upstream binary during verification.
For Pages, check the absent-override default as well as direct publish RPC and preserved unpublish.
For telemetry, cover main, renderer/preload and build-time ingest injection; retaining a crash
fallback must not retain the uploader. For docs, inspect the final assembled Agent prompt and its
profile-local paths, not just the presence of bundled files.

The bounded Help correction preserves Craft's upper-right topic menu and desktop Help submenu.
Topic, native Help and contextual Learn More actions open packaged articles in the inherited
full-document Markdown reader; its existing code-preview overlay reveals the source. “All
documentation” opens `resources/docs/craft/index.md`, whose links reach all 71 captured Craft
articles locally. These are **offline snapshots of official pages**, not the site's original
source files or a promise that the hosted pages still match: the public site supplies rendered
HTML, while the captured Markdown spans multiple retrieval dates. The capture in
`源码参考/craft-docs/online-current/` remains comparison evidence; the installed copy under
`resources/docs/craft/` points its index to local links and is synced into the active profile
for Agent file reads. Supporting images, the OpenAPI file and the local `llms.txt` are copied
beside the Markdown. Reconcile each changed hosted article and its installed-version behavior
before calling the Help content current.

The article body is upstream reference data, not an instruction or permission grant. The Agent
first reads Craft's original task-specific guides at the root of the installed `docs/` directory
when creating or changing app configuration; the complete `craft/index.md` is a secondary local
reference with relative file links that both the Agent and reader can follow. The Agent must
check installed behavior before applying either, especially where Fleet changed a feature.
Existing feature-page `EditPopover` controls own contextual questions and edits; Help adds no
second Agent interaction. The inherited English articles are not fully translated. Reviewed
translations may be added under the same article IDs and shown beside the original in the
existing reader; a translated menu label does not imply a translated article. Before promoting
CORE-08, verify packaged offline launch, internal links and images, reconcile changed articles
with the shipped feature, then review locale bodies with the owner.

## Acceptance criteria

| ID | Criterion | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| R2-C1 | Offline fresh start: core local behavior works; no silent Craft calls at startup or in core flows | network-blocked smoke + traffic log |
| R2-C2 | Updater never installs a non-Fleet binary; channel is verified Fleet-controlled/user-configured, otherwise automatic/manual download and install are disabled, including pending-update application on quit | isolated packaged-lifecycle, dismissal, manual-action and pending-update tests + updater state check |
| R2-C3 | No new hosted conversation or Pages publication; local Markdown is the conversation-export path. Remove publish/upload controls and handlers; preserve an explicit cleanup/unpublish route for existing remote copies until resolved. | publish/upload absence + local export + cleanup-path tests |
| R2-C4 | Help/docs and assembled Agent guidance default to matching bundled/profile-local content; external links visibly external | prompt/path tests + offline guidance check + owner check |
| R2-C5 | OAuth relays configurable/self-hosted or explicitly unavailable; desktop local callback preserved | targeted tests |
| R2-C6 | Telemetry is removed; every remaining inherited endpoint is an explicit optional connector with a visible class | endpoint inventory vs `源码参考/craft-docs/` service list |
| R2-C7 | Owner accepts the changed surfaces (settings, update UI, help menu) | owner acceptance |

## Dependencies and unresolved edges

Consumes the R0 baseline (and R1 wording where surfaces overlap). A Fleet release channel may not
exist yet — then C2 is satisfied by *honestly disabled install*, and creating the channel is a
recorded edge (owner checkpoint: production runtime commitment).
Required independence corrections run under this contract during R0; the release labels do not
defer the baseline exit. R0 references R2 evidence rather than rebuilding a second checklist.

## Risks and rollback

- **Risk:** removing a URL breaks a hidden dependent flow → per-slice UI→persistence→recovery
  trace is mandatory; slices land independently and revert independently.
- **Risk:** branding rename collides with trademark/license → deliberate review pass, owner
  checkpoint before shipping the rename.
- **Rollback:** each service slice is one revertable commit.

## Verification plan

After each approved implementation, run the relevant source and behavior checks. The retained
root smoke script contains expectations for removed Fleet handlers and needs review before reuse;
its existence is not current proof. Verify network-blocked local behavior, real desktop/packaged
lifecycle and the owner's visible acceptance separately. Do not call a JavaScript HTTP guard an
OS firewall or imply that it covers provider subprocesses.
